# Recreation Prompt

Create a portrait-first browser sniper game titled **No-Scope Multiverse: Aftershift Board**. Preserve the original mechanics exactly: start menu, mouse/touch aim, one tap/click fires, 10 ammo, targets spawn in a 3x4 grid, five standard target hits unlock a boss, boss hit wins, boss timeout or out-of-ammo fails, restart resets. Transform the presentation into a satirical cyber-comic sniper game with chrome aesthetic, neon cyberpunk palette, fps/shooter hooks, after-work leaderboard energy, and meme-tone copy such as no-scope and main character. Use procedural canvas art for a chrome portal tower, glitch variants, a Main Character boss, particles, and a web-like sniper scope. Keep UI readable and tappable on 4:7 to 9:16 mobile portrait screens.
blueprint_markdown:
# Blueprint

## Source truth
The preserved reference (`index_old.html`) is a browser-native canvas sniper game. The player starts from a menu, aims a smoothed scope with mouse/touch, fires one shot per click/tap, has 10 ammo, and eliminates pop-up targets in a 3x4 window grid. Five standard targets must be eliminated before a boss/commander can appear. Hitting the boss wins; letting the boss time out or exhausting ammo after a miss fails. Restart resets all state.

## Protected mechanics
- One-thumb/mouse aim controls with canvas-scoped touch prevention.
- Click/tap-to-fire input semantics.
- 10 ammo, no reload, low-ammo warning only as feedback.
- 12 target windows, up to 3 visible targets, random timed spawns.
- 5 standard target eliminations unlock boss eligibility.
- Circular hit detection around target head with roughly the same threshold.
- Boss timeout and ammo exhaustion failure; boss hit victory; restart flow.

## Transformable surfaces
Title, HUD terms, target and boss identities, background scene, window rendering, reticle styling, particles, feedback copy, audio selection, typography, panel styling, and progression language are presentation surfaces and safe to transform.

## Target remix
**No-Scope Multiverse: Aftershift Board** reframes the loop as a satirical cyber-comic sniper game inspired by multiverse animation language without copying protected IP. The player operates a chrome Main-Character Lens after work, sniping glitch variants to expose an overconfident Main Character anomaly and climb an intentionally fake leaderboard.
